the extent to which DNA coding for maternal RNAs is conserved during evolution is greater than that of single-copy DNA, that the DNA coding for maternal mRNAs is more highly conserved than DNA coding for other types of maternal RNAs, and that the DNA coding of maternal mRNAs and the DNA coding of other maternal RNAs are more highly conserved during evolution than the DNA coding for proteins.
